question: Why do the primaries matter?
answer: In blue states and districts, the primary election *is* the main election. The winner of many of the primaries are expected to win the general election come November. So, the primary is important as it is our chance to put true progressives on the November ballot in place of (often incumbent) do-nothing-Dems who would not generate the positive change we need to see in our communities.

question: How do I vote in the primaries?
answer: If you haven't already recieved a mail in ballot, you can go in person to a polling center and pick up a ballot, or vote in person on June 30th. If you're not registered yet, you will need your: name, birthday, address, and a Drivers License number, State ID number, or SSN. \n Useful links: [Check/Update: tr.ee/co_voter](tr.ee/co_voter) / [Register: tr.ee/co_new_voter](tr.ee/co_new_voter)
